components.basis: All three listed subcomponents (GOAL-01, GOAL-02, GOAL-03) are covered (see their entries). Standing: the body theorem carries proved=annex:p2.fol.clausal.composition and the annex item (annex 107-176) writes the composition proof step by step, resting only on on-route proved results (prenex theorem and its lemmas, Skolem theorem, matrix lemma with its own annex proof 71-105). The original note 'currently left to an exercise' is answered: the result is no longer an exercise. Hypotheses kept: sentence input with the open-formula closure caveat (supplement 237-239, annex 174), nonempty-domain semantics (supplement 4-5, 104), AC confined to the forward Skolem expansion (supplement 118-121). No narrower substituted claim found.

The declared input is an arbitrary first-order L-sentence (supplement 117), with the semantics fixed at 4-5 and the closure requirement for open formulas at 237-239. The theorem (116-125) states the whole pipeline as the composition of Table tab:p02-fol-normal-form-pipeline along its CNF branch: NNF, rectified NNF, prenex NNF, universal Skolem sentence, CNF matrix, clause set (rows 1-5 and 7, 141-169; row 6 DNF marked as comparison only), repeated as Figure fig:p02-fol-normal-form-pipeline (183-201) and instantiated in the worked example (218-236). Output: a finite set of universally read clauses in a finite expansion L*.

Composition written in annex 109-174: prenex conversion (NNF, rectification, prenex extraction via thm:prenex-normal-form and lem:fol-nnf, 110-119), then Skolemization of that rectified prenex sentence (121-133), then S = Cl(theta) by the distributive clause construction (135-140; definition supplement 81-101, lemma 103-114 with annex proof 71-105), then the clause-closure argument (142-163) and both satisfiability directions (165-174). Freshness/signature changes explicit at every stage: NNF, rectification and prenex add no nonlogical symbol and use a fixed infinite variable enumeration (annex 116-118; fresh binder = least variable outside V, restoration 125-126; table row 2 'fresh binders are chosen outside a finite forbidden set'); Skolem adds one fresh function symbol per existential position, arity zero for an initial existential, terms over preceding universal variables only, signature L -> finite expansion L* (annex 122-129; restoration 290-301; table row 4); the expansion interprets f_j by the chosen F_j (restoration 390-391); clause conversion stays in L* and adds no symbol or variable (annex 139-140; supplement 96-98, 112), contrasted with Tseitin (table row 5).

Directions stated correctly: forward, a model of sigma has an expansion to L* satisfying the Skolem sentence, using AC (restoration 320-322; annex 130-131; supplement 118-119); reverse, the L-reduct of a model satisfies sigma without choice (restoration 323-324, 326-328; annex 132-133, 168-171; supplement 119-121). Only the Skolem step is labelled expansion-reduct equisatisfiability, 'not same-signature formula equivalence' (supplement 123-124, table row 4 at 152-157, figure caption 203-206, restoration remark 432-435, annex 173-174). Same-signature steps are claimed as formula equivalence (rows 1-3, 5); the clause-set step is claimed as equality of models via universal closures, not formula-string equivalence (row 7 at 166-169, figure 200-201 and caption, supplement 212-216), and is proved in annex 142-163. No formula equivalence is asserted where only satisfiability transfers.
